description: react-component-development is targeted against three route components that each hand-roll their own loading and error branches in three different shapes — PostListPage.tsx inline, PostEditorPage.tsx by early return, RootRedirect.tsx by early return that renders nothing at all while pending — with code-maintainability (a general-quality read of the same repetition) and react-component-styling (a misroute, since nothing about the repetition is CSS) sitting in the peer set as competing, plausible-looking picks, which is what makes the discovery factor a real question rather than a formality. The outcome factors check that the repeated concern lands in one new module both PostListPage.tsx and PostEditorPage.tsx import, and that the extraction still lets each screen say its own thing rather than flattening both onto one hardcoded message. Neither factor asserts role="alert" or any other semantic or keyboard detail: react-component-development's own SKILL.md defers semantics and keyboard behaviour to a high-fidelity UI design capability, and none is in this scenario's peer set, so asserting one would measure accessibility instinct with nothing to attribute the result to.

task.prompt: Right now every screen in the console handles "still loading" and "that didn't work" in its own way — the post list prints one sentence, the editor replaces the whole screen with a different one, and opening the app shows nothing at all for a moment. None of them quite matches the others. We're adding a couple more screens soon and I'd rather each one didn't invent its own version of this all over again.

factors.description: The ask names neither react-component-development nor the mechanism a fix would use, only three screens that each handle "still loading" and "that didn't work" differently — an agent that reaches for react-component-development here is finding it from the problem, with code-maintainability (a general-quality read of the same repetition) and react-component-styling (a misroute, since nothing about the repetition is CSS) sitting right there as competing, plausible-looking picks.

Reads PostListPage.tsx and PostEditorPage.tsx from the reconstructed workspace, resolves each file's relative imports, and takes the SET of resolved modules imported by both that are also files this probe's own diff added. Requires that set to be actually about loading and error, reading two sources together rather than any one file alone: each module's own effective text, AND — for each route file — the JSX usage span of every name it binds from a module in the set, so a shared surface that takes its content entirely from its callers (carrying no loading/error vocabulary in its own file by design) still qualifies through how each screen actually invokes it. The check looks for a loading-ish token (pending/loading/waiting/busy/fetching/spinner/skeleton) and a failure-ish token (isError/hasError/failure/problem/retry/alert/a rendered role="alert", among others — never a bare "error", which almost any module contains unrelated to this concern), tested against that combined text AND a second copy with a space inserted at every camelCase/PascalCase boundary, so a token FUSED into an identifier (a component literally named LoadingError, never rendering the word "loading" itself) counts the same as the word set apart by real whitespace. Two focused components — a Spinner and a separate ErrorBanner, each newly added and shared — satisfy this exactly as well as one combined component does. A module that is nothing but a bare re-export is read as the file it names instead, one hop; a module this cannot fully resolve counts in its favour rather than against it; a shared surface used as a wrapper around genuinely different children can absorb THEIR vocabulary as if it were its own; and a module that merely references both concerns without truly consolidating them can pass on lexical presence alone — all deliberate: a false negative here rejects a probe that extracted correctly, landing specifically on the skill-present arm, the worse of this instrument's two possible errors; a false positive costs one over-generous verdict, symmetric across both conditions. A shared .module.css never counts, since a stylesheet says nothing about the repeated BEHAVIOUR this scenario is about. A generic data-fetching wrapper both screens merely CALL (never render as JSX), with each screen's own loading/error JSX left untouched and inline, still fails it, since a call contributes no usage span of its own. Two screens that each grew their own helper, introduced no new file, or share a module unrelated to loading and error all still fail it. A route file missing from the workspace is a judgment this script cannot make, so it exits non-zero rather than reporting false.

The paired "must not disappear" factor. react-component-development's own component-states.md has the shared surface take its content from the caller so features "keep their distinct control without forking the surface"; an extraction that renders one hardcoded message on both screens has moved the duplication rather than removed it. The script finds the same shared, newly-added module SET the factor above detects — including through that factor's own widened read, each module's own text plus each route's JSX usage span of what it imports from the set, tested together with a camelCase/PascalCase-un-fused copy so a vocabulary token fused into an identifier still registers — then reads each screen's own usage of every module in that set, and reports false when the two screens' combined usage is identical once each screen's own pre-existing query-variable name is normalized away — including when there is no such module set to parameterize at all. It is deliberately not independent of the factor above, judging the quality of the extraction that factor detects, so a run that changed nothing also passes it — the same reason keeps-the-detail-cache-write and keeps-the-animation-for-everyone-else are declared as pairs for their own scenarios. It inherits that factor's own permissive bias, the worse mistake being a false negative that rejects a probe which really did extract correctly: a module accepted on lexical presence alone, without truly consolidating the concern — including a wrapper whose only vocabulary came from children it merely renders around — is still compared for usage the same as any other.
